title: The nervous system in your gut
summary: Your digestive tract is lined with the enteric nervous system — over 100 million nerve cells that can run digestion on their own and constantly signal the brain.
evidenceNote: The enteric nervous system and its independence are well established. Claims about the gut shaping mood are an active research area and often overstated.

scenes.text: You have a nervous system in your gut.
The enteric nervous system is a mesh of nerve cells lining your digestive tract, from esophagus to rectum.
It contains more than 100 million nerve cells — some estimates go much higher.
It can coordinate digestion even without instructions from the brain.
scenes.reveal: That's why it's nicknamed the 'second brain' — though it doesn't think.

left.label: Brain → gut
left.text: Stress can speed up or slow down digestion

right.label: Gut → brain
right.text: Most vagus nerve fibres carry signals upward

scenes.text: Butterflies in your stomach are a real two-way conversation.
